title: Corporations Regextable
text: vignette demonstrates extract mentions corporations using regex lookup table corporation names, aliases, tickers, metadata. regextable::extract() workflow allows consistent identification corporation names across datasets, even multiple aliases variants used. Install load package:
code: library(regextable) library(kableExtra) library(rvest) library(pbapply) library(purrr) library(tibble) library(stringr)

title: Corporations Regextable
text: corporations_regex table contains sample corporations, common aliases, ticker symbols, reference sources used matching standardization. aliases column includes alternative names, abbreviations, common variants corporation ensure comprehensive matching.
code: corporations_regex <- read.csv("/Users/shirl/Downloads/corporations_regex.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) kable(head(corporations_regex))

title: Corporations Regextable
text: following dataset contains organizations contributors involved Project 2025. used demonstrate matching standardizing corporation names using regex table.
code: project_2025_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/judgelord/corporations/main/data/project_2025_coalition_and_contributors.rda" tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rda") download.file(project_2025_url, tmp, mode = "wb") load(tmp) kable(head(project_2025_coalition_and_contributors))

title: Corporations Regextable
text: extract() function searches organization column dataset using aliases patterns regex table. returns standardized corporation names optionally removing acronym-matches reduce false positives.
code: corp_df <- extract(data = project_2025_coalition_and_contributors,                    col_name = "organization",                    regex_table = corporations_regex,                    data_return_cols = "organization",                    remove_acronyms = TRUE,                    use_ner = TRUE)  kable(head(corp_df))

title: Native American Tribes Regex Table
text: demonstrate extraction, vignette collects tribe names National Congress American Indians (NCAI) Tribal Directory. directory provides publicly available information federally recognized tribes.
code: max_page <- read_html("https://www.ncai.org/tribal-directory") %>%   html_elements(".Pagination_numberButton__vLhpm") %>%   html_text() %>%   as.numeric() %>%   max(na.rm = TRUE)  all_pages <- paste0("https://www.ncai.org/tribal-directory/page/", 1:max_page)  tribes_df <- map_df(all_pages, function(url) {      message("Scraping: ", url)   html <- read_html(url)   cards <- html %>% html_elements("article.TribeCard_tribeCard__UJcdx")      map_df(cards, function(card) {     tibble(       Region = card %>% html_element(".TribeCard_regionLabel___OVFL")                      %>% html_text(trim = TRUE)                      %>% str_remove(" Region"),       Tribe = card %>% html_element("h2") %>% html_text(trim = TRUE),       Leader = card %>% html_element("section:nth-of-type(1) p:nth-of-type(1)")                      %>% html_text(trim = TRUE),       Tel = card %>% html_element(xpath = ".//p[strong[contains(., 'Tel:')]]")                   %>% html_text(trim = TRUE)                   %>% str_remove("Tel: "),       Fax = card %>% html_element(xpath = ".//p[strong[contains(., 'Fax:')]]")                   %>% html_text(trim = TRUE)                   %>% str_remove("Fax: "),       Address = card %>% html_element("section:nth-of-type(2)") %>% html_text2(),       Recognition = card %>% html_element(".TribeCard_federal__bQB0g")                           %>% html_text(trim = TRUE),       District = card %>% html_element(".TribeCard_generic__MLwRU")                        %>% html_text(trim = TRUE)                       %>% str_remove("Congressional District ")     )   }) })  kable(head(tribes_df))

title: Native American Tribes Regex Table
text: example demonstrates use regextable::extract() extract Native American Tribe names Tribal Directory data (tribes_df). extract() function searches Tribe column using regex patterns Strings column tribes_regex. match found, function returns original tribe name along metadata regex table, source reference.
code: tribe_directory_df <- extract(     data = tribes_df,     regex_table = tribes_regex,     col_name = "Tribe",     pattern_col = "Strings",     data_return_cols = "Tribe",     regex_return_cols = "Source" )  kable(head(tribe_directory_df))

title: regextable
text: regextable extracts regex-based pattern matches data frame character vector using pattern lookup table. input row, matching patterns returned, along matched substring, internal row identifier, additional columns specified data_return_cols regex_return_cols. Optional metadata pattern table can also included. Multiple rows may returned single text matches multiple patterns. function also supports additional parameters do_clean_text, unique_match, verbose, cl. can used control text cleaning, limit matches per row, show progress messages, speed processing large datasets. Install load package:
code: library(regextable) library(kableExtra)

title: regextable
text: demonstration, use two included datasets: members: lookup table regex patterns member names. cr2007_03_01: sample text dataset search.
code: data("members") kable(members) data("cr2007_03_01") kable(cr2007_03_01)

title: regextable
text: extract() performs basic text cleaning default - standardizing spaces, punctuation, capitalization—improve pattern matching. can disabled setting do_clean_text = FALSE. Cleaning standardizes spacing, punctuation, capitalization, helps regex pattern matching. Example clean_text():
code: text <- "  HELLO---WORLD  " clean_text(text) #> [1] "hello world"

title: regextable
text: simplest use extract(): Explanation: - data: text dataset search. - col_name: column contains text. - regex_table: lookup table patterns. - data_return_cols: additional columns data include result. - regex_return_cols: additional columns pattern table attach. row output corresponds detected match, includes original text matching pattern. —
code: result <- regextable::extract(   data = cr2007_03_01,   regex_table = members,   data_return_cols = c("text"),   regex_return_cols = c("icpsr") )  kable(head(result))

title: regextable
text: extract() can also filter data date, remove acronyms (-uppercase patterns 2+ characters), select specific output columns. useful controlled extraction. Explanation: - date_col, date_start, date_end: filter rows date. - remove_acronyms: skip patterns like “NASA” “USA”. can combine filters subset columns flexible outputs. —

title: regextable
text: extract() supports parallel processing via cl parameter:
code: library(parallel) clust <- makeCluster(2) result_parallel <- regextable::extract(   data = cr2007_03_01,   regex_table = members,   cl = clust,   data_return_cols = c("text"),   regex_return_cols = c("icpsr") ) stopCluster(clust) kable(head(result_parallel))

title: regextable
text: matching, default, clean_text() applied standardize text better matching messy text. converts text lowercase, removes excess punctuation, replaces line breaks dashes spaces, collapses multiple spaces single space. Text cleaning applied matching modify original input data. Users can disable behavior setting do_clean_text = FALSE.
code: text <- "  HELLO---WORLD  " cleaned_text <- clean_text(text) print(cleaned_text) #> [1] "hello world"

title: regextable
text: extract() performs regex-based matching text column using pattern lookup table. patterns match row returned, along corresponding pattern optional metadata pattern table. multiple patterns match text, multiple rows returned, one per match.

title: regextable
text: data: data frame character vector containing text search. regex_table: regex lookup table least one pattern column.

title: regextable
text: col_name: (default "text") Column name data frame containing text search . pattern_col: (default "pattern") Name regex pattern column regex_table. data_return_cols: (default NULL) Vector additional columns data include output. regex_return_cols: (default NULL) Vector additional columns regex_table include output. date_col: (default NULL) Column data containing dates filtering. date_start: (default NULL) Start date filtering rows. date_end: (default NULL) End date filtering rows. remove_acronyms: (default FALSE) TRUE, removes -uppercase patterns regex_table. do_clean_text: (default TRUE) TRUE, cleans text matching. verbose: (default TRUE) TRUE, displays progress messages. unique_match (default FALSE) TRUE, stops searching first match find one match per row. cl: (default NULL) cluster object integer specifying child processes parallel evaluation (ignored Windows).

title: Extract pattern matches from text — extract
text: Pattern matching performed using R's regular expression engine case-insensitive default. input row, function checks patterns regex_table returns matches based unique_match parameter.

title: Extract pattern matches from text — extract
code: # Create sample data data <- data.frame(   id = 1:3,   text = c("I love apples", "Bananas are great", "Oranges and apples"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Create regex patterns patterns <- data.frame(   pattern = c("apples", "bananas", "oranges"),   category = c("fruit", "fruit", "fruit") )  # Extract all matches extract(data, "text", patterns) #> Scanning 3 patterns against 3 text entries... #>    |                                                  | 0 % ~calculating     |+++++++++++++++++                                 | 33% ~00s             |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++                | 67% ~00s             |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++| 100% elapsed=00s   #> Number of rows with matches: 4 #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>   row_id pattern match   #>    <int> <chr>   <chr>   #> 1      1 apples  apples  #> 2      2 bananas Bananas #> 3      3 apples  apples  #> 4      3 oranges Oranges  # Extract one match per row extract(data, "text", patterns, unique_match = TRUE) #> Scanning: 3 patterns against 3 text entries... #>    |                                                  | 0 % ~calculating     |+++++++++++++++++                                 | 33% ~00s             |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++                | 67% ~00s             |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++| 100% elapsed=00s   #> Number of rows with matches: 3 #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   row_id pattern match   #>    <int> <chr>   <chr>   #> 1      1 apples  apples  #> 2      2 bananas Bananas #> 3      3 apples  apples
